claims.statement: SesamCmdClient.test directly uploads once, waits for deployment, calls run for args.runs cycles (default 1), and verifies once after all cycles; it retains only the last run's additional_info and re-raises stage failures, preventing subsequent stages.
The test dispatcher calls test() directly and therefore does not execute the connector upload dispatcher's expansion, validation, directory changes, or optional authentication prelude.

Upload reads the profile before optional sink deletion, replaces environment before configuration, waits for deployment before uploading testdata, and has no rollback of earlier successful remote writes when a later stage fails.

Testdata upload discovers JSON files recursively, derives receiver pipe IDs from filenames, filters jobs by a nonempty pipe whitelist, aggregates parallel failures into TestDataUploadException, and fails fast in the sequential path; the parallel success log's five-second wait has no matching sleep.

Upload defaults to the test profile and disables ordinary user-pipe scheduling through node metadata unless enable_user_pipes is set; passing enable_user_pipes to run alone does not change that metadata.

upload_delete_sink_datasets deletes existing sink datasets before environment/config replacement, including when test calls upload; its help warns of greater residual-data/config influence compared with wipe/reset.

Deployment waiting selects user pipes in runtime state Deploying, sleeps five seconds between attempts, defaults to a 30-minute timeout, and catches BaseException around individual deployment checks; it does not establish pipe validity or output correctness.

Only validate and format are classified as offline by CLI startup; run, test, verify, update, stop, and run-pytest resolve node/JWT, construct SesamNode, and require developer mode, while non-developer force overrides are limited to upload/download.

run stops the previous scheduler before starting a new internal run, and a stop exception prevents startup; the stop wrapper POSTs stop-run-all-pipes with terminate_timeout 30 and checks HTTP status, but the stop command does not inspect a success field in returned JSON.

Run delegates stabilization and pipe execution to the node's run-all-pipes endpoint rather than implementing scheduling, change detection, reset behavior, or timeout enforcement locally; documented stabilization intent is interpreted through backend terminal status.

The scheduler CLI defaults are zero-runs 2, max-runs 100, max-run-time 900 seconds, and request-mode sync; these become extra_zero_runs, max_runs, max_run_time, and request_mode query parameters. Scheduler mode is locally None and omitted unless supplied, although help advertises active as default; the handler validates active/poll and sync/async.

Scheduler input-dataset deletion depends only on whether testdata is a directory in the current working directory: even an empty directory sends delete_input_datasets=False; otherwise the client omits the parameter and relies on the backend true default.

The scheduler request normally omits reset_pipes_and_delete_sink_datasets, sends False when scheduler_dont_reset_pipes_or_delete_sink_datasets is enabled, and sends check_input_pipes/output_run_statistics only when enabled; option help identifies input-pipe checking as a control on run failure.

dont_remove_scheduler, use_internal_scheduler, custom_scheduler, scheduler_image_tag, scheduler_id, scheduler_node, scheduler_poll_frequency, and compact_execution_datasets are parsed compatibility options without behavior-reading consumers in the run/stop handlers; they neither select a separate scheduler implementation nor change cleanup or polling sleeps.

A SchedulerRunner thread issues run-all-pipes; sync response status success becomes local finished and any other status becomes failed, while exceptions in the worker become failed with the exception stored as its result.

Async scheduler execution requires an initial token and polls get-pipe-runner-status with it, registering user interaction each time; success finishes, failed or not-running fails, other statuses continue after ten seconds, and a missing token or polling exception fails the worker.

The main scheduler wait uses one-second sleeps and optional get-run-all-pipes-log calls with available token and since cursor; it advances the cursor from dictionary log timestamps and fetches again on terminal status. Sync has no assigned token, and log-fetch exceptions can abort the main wait outside worker exception handling.

A failed scheduler runner raises RuntimeError with its result and prevents test verification; successful runs log duration and return additional_info from the initial run response, which async terminal status polling does not replace.

run, test, and scheduler waiting provide no general finally-based stop or rollback after errors or interruption; the worker only records exceptions and the outer CLI finally only logs duration, so explicit stop may be needed after reconnecting and does not undo earlier mutations.

TestSpec discovery reads only top-level expected/*.test.json as utf-8-sig JSON objects, rejects non-objects, merges supplied keys over constructor defaults without general schema validation, and groups multiple specs per pipe.

TestSpec defaults derive name from the filename without .test.json, file from the initial name plus .json, pipe from its final path component, and endpoint json; ordinary relative expected paths are prefixed with expected, while ignore defaults false and ignore_deletes defaults true with literal-true checks.

TestSpec stage, parameters, and blacklist default to None, fields_to_sort_by defaults to _id, and the constructor does not synthesize the README's advertised _id/type defaults; _id, type, and description do not select execution or comparison counts.

Pipe classification checks effective configuration in order: embedded source is input, sink type ending _endpoint is endpoint, dataset source plus dataset sink is internal, absent sink dataset is output, otherwise internal; user filtering excludes specified system origins and IDs containing :singlenode.

Verify considers only output and endpoint user pipes and logs/excludes pipes without true is-valid-config, without marking failure solely for that exclusion; referenced excluded pipes then fail spec eligibility. Update collects output and endpoint pipes without the same validity filter.

A nonempty pipe whitelist derived from pipes/...conf.json entries filters TestSpecs, verification, update maintenance, and testdata jobs; empty pipe lists do not activate those checks, and the whitelist is not sent to the run-all-pipes request.
The single option is advertised for single-pipe verify/update but neither handler nor TestSpec loading applies it.
When no TestSpecs remain after loading, verify warns and returns before checking for unreferenced output pipes, so successful test completion can occur without any output comparisons.

Verify's loader fails for a non-ignored spec with a missing expected file or any spec referencing an absent eligible pipe, including an ignored spec; these loader failures differ from the later Verify failed error for mismatches or unreferenced eligible pipes when some specs exist.

Ignored specs skip comparison and permit missing expected files; normally verify warns about an existing ignored output file, while update deletes that file and skips fetching/writing. The ignored-file warning/removal branch is gated on no prior loader failure.

Update creates placeholder [] newline files for missing expected output and empty specs for eligible whitelisted pipes lacking specs, then writes fetched output; if no specs remain after generation it raises an assertion.

Update deletes non-ignored specs referencing absent eligible pipes but does not delete their expected output files; ignored absent-pipe specs are retained with a warning, and whitelisted-away specs bypass this maintenance.

JSON and excel TestSpecs fetch entity JSON from /pipes/<pipe>/entities with an optional stage query rather than downloading publisher output or Excel bytes; parameters are used only for publisher endpoints.
Reading published output can enable a disabled pipe pump before the request and does not restore its prior disabled state.

Entity filtering deep-copies nested dictionaries/lists, applies blacklists first, and removes underscore-prefixed keys except _id and literal-true _deleted; false _deleted is removed, blacklist can remove retained keys, and retained _id/true _deleted values are not recursively filtered.

Blacklist matching uses fnmatch on dot-joined property paths with generated backslash-dot escapes removed and pattern []. replaced by .*.; dictionary recursion adds keys but list recursion adds no index segment, and literal dotted keys are not distinguished from equivalent nested paths.

Entity sorting uses configured fields_to_sort_by or _id, serializes dictionary field values with sorted keys, and appends whole-entity sorted-key JSON as a tie-breaker; other key values remain native, nested list order is unchanged, and incompatible sort-key types are not universally normalized.

Current entity number normalization recursively converts Decimal/float values only when their string ends in .0 and, unless no_large_int_bugs is enabled, converts integers through float/Decimal when their string length exceeds that of 9007199254740991; this compatibility condition is not an exact numeric safe-integer threshold.

JSON/excel verification sorts expected entities but filters and numerically normalizes only current entities, sorts current again after normalization, and compares lengths plus sorted-key JSON serialization with ensure_ascii false; mismatches produce diagnostic output/diffs and ultimately fail verification.

For entity endpoints, ignore_deletes true drops unexpected current tombstones during verify but retains tombstones whose IDs are expected deletions; update with that same default drops all tombstones, while false includes all filtered tombstones in both operations.

CSV and other non-JSON/non-excel/non-XML endpoints compare raw expected and publisher bytes without entity filtering, sorting, numeric or delete normalization; UTF-8 then Latin-1 decoding is attempted only for mismatch diagnostics.

XML verification intends prettified string comparison through bytes_to_xml_string, which explicitly calls self.find_xml_header_settings(xml_data); the helper exists under that name but its quoted standalone slicing drops the final character and returns a string to serialization, so the inspected implementation does not establish reliable XML normalization.

XML verification catches BaseException around conversion/comparison and attempts a byte fallback that can conceal helper/serializer errors; sequential reassignment can leave a string-versus-bytes comparison if only expected conversion succeeds. XML update uses the same header helper to pretty-print UTF-8 and has no corresponding byte fallback.

Update fetches current output without running or uploading first and performs loader file maintenance before fetches; expected writes create/truncate files without creating parent directories or providing a transaction across specs, so failures can leave partial baseline/spec changes.

JSON/excel update filters and normalizes current entities, applies its deletion policy and sorting, then writes two-space sorted-key JSON plus newline as UTF-8; unicode_encoding enables Unicode escapes and default HTML escaping replaces less-than, greater-than, and ampersand unless disable_json_html_escape is set. Other publisher types are stored as bytes, except XML's separate formatting branch.

Verify summary counts and its failure denominator use the number of pipe keys rather than individual specs/comparisons, while update counts processed non-ignored specs, so multiple specs per pipe and ignored specs can make the reported counts misleading as comparison totals.

Post-command pytest runs only after successful command dispatch, outside test(); test may already log success before pytest fails. The hook applies to commands other than run-pytest with a supplied folder and suppresses the recent-upload/run warning only for test.

Standalone run-pytest requires a positional folder, takes the first remaining command argument as that folder, runs with the standalone warning, and is excluded from the post-command hook to avoid a second invocation.

The pytest runner checks only top-level test_*.py before invocation and warns/returns if none exist; otherwise pytest receives the folder plus ordinary whitespace-split pytest_args, default -rP -v, without shell/shlex interpretation of embedded quotes.

Pytest exit value zero is success and any other value raises RuntimeError; the CLI converts the failure to exit 1 rather than preserving pytest's particular exit code, and pytest.main does not sandbox test side effects.

The fair-weather scenario invokes reset, whitelisted test with scheduler logs and post-command pytest, update, status, download with ZIP dump, and final reset; its authored specs cover default entity JSON and explicit CSV bytes under default sync scheduling, not async/XML or custom normalization/failure branches.
Fair-weather's CSV fixture uses CRLF expected bytes and a csv_endpoint sink with _id/name columns, while its default JSON spec reads entities from a pipe with an http_endpoint sink.

The embedded-conversion scenario copies fixtures to scratch, wipes, converts, runs test with extracted testdata and scheduler logs, resets, and compares the whole tree; its only output TestSpec targets output-pipe, so remote output verification does not independently cover every extracted input's downstream output.
The authored naming pytest checks only that local pipe filenames and JSON _id values contain no underscores; it neither exercises CLI handlers nor checks filename/ID equality or lowercase naming.

Both shell scenarios use set -e and retry whole commands up to three total attempts with 15-second delays, and their normal-path final resets are not guaranteed after earlier failure because neither installs a cleanup trap; these retries are distinct from per-file testdata retries.

Integration CI serializes its OS matrix because the jobs share a remote node; the test driver supplies that node and credential to both authored shell scenarios, so they are credentialed state-changing integration checks rather than offline tests.
